name: Bookmarks and reading list
plain: Sites cannot read your bookmarks or reading list.
meaning: Only browser extensions with the bookmarks permission can read them. A web page has no API at all; even installing a PWA is detectable only through display-mode.

access.persistence: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored
access.iframe: Readable from cross-origin iframes too (same values)

fields.name: proxy: display-mode standalone
fields.range: page knows if it was launched as an installed app

fields.name: proxy: beforeinstallprompt event
fields.range: shows the page is installable, not bookmarks

story.what_it_is: Sites cannot read your bookmarks or reading list.
story.for_you: Your saved sites stay between you and your browser. A web page has no way to look at them. Only a browser extension you install and allow can.
story.for_makers: Sites would love to know what you save, because it shows your real interests. The web gives no such access. They can only see how you arrive and, with an installed web app, how you launch it.

use_cases.example: A shop wanted to know whether you bookmarked it, to see loyalty. It must use sign-in and repeat visits instead.
A publisher wanted your saved articles, and instead offers its own Save for later button.
A read it later site wants your reading list, so it asks you to import a file or use an extension.
An advertiser wanted bookmarks for interest data, which are not available to pages.
A product team wants to know who bookmarked the page and settles for return visits.
A tracker wanted to link your saved sites to a profile, which the browser blocks.
A game site wanted to remind you to come back, so it asks you to install the web app instead.

risks: Only extensions you install can read them

legit_uses: None: the browser deliberately withholds it
abuse: Sites attempt proxies to recover it
